correctness.rationale: For leaf-star distances d_ij=a_i+a_j, Kantorovich-Rubinstein dual norm of each zero-total-mass signed measure equals sum a_i|mu_i|. Thus for any real signed extension weights sum u=1, new-point seminorm is max_j Phi_j/R with Phi_j=a_j|1-u_j|+sum_{k != j}a_k|u_k|, and original pair distances add floor 1. For t<=t_c=(m-2)/m, averaging long-leaf dual inequalities yields a global supporting hyperplane max Phi>=1+t, with equality uniquely concentrated on short leaf below threshold and exactly an all-equal long-coefficient line segment at threshold. For t>t_c, positive dual multipliers q=(1+t)/(2(mt+1)) and s=(mt-m+2)/(2(mt+1)) give a common subgradient and sharp value m(1+t)^2/[2(mt+1)], and equality forces all signed optimum weights positive and unique. For R>T, inequalities Phi_j<=R give a full-dimensional compact optimal polytope; R<=T classifications hold even with signed coefficients. Independently solved unrestricted signed LP for m=3..7 and selected t values, confirming exact formulas and optimizer phases; finite checks only supplement all-real proof.
